newsitem.title: USA: US debt futures end lower in profit-taking setback.
newsitem.headline: US debt futures end lower in profit-taking setback.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended solidly lower Friday after a jab above the lofty 115-00 level in September bonds the day before inspired profit-taking.

Anticipation of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's semiannual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony next week and the midday expiration of August Treasury options derailed the ongoing rally after bonds reached a new seven-month high of 115-02 on Thursday, floor traders said.
"I don't think people want to be long going into Greenspan," said one bond floor broker.

Many traders said they had expected a profit-taking wave before the weekend. After the initial drop, selling interest largely dried up and prices wallowed a few ticks above the 114-01 session low for the rest of the day.
"It just kind of fizzled," said a trader.
Traders said a 100-point plus intraday plunge in the Dow Jones Industrial Average contributed psychological pressure to bonds. The DJIA has since recovered somewhat to trade down 70 points at 7950.

The University of Michigan consumer sentiment survey was stronger than expected in July at 106.4 versus June's 104.5 and the 104.6 forecast. However, traders noted bonds' direction had been largely determined before the report.

May U.S. trade data also had a neglible effect on bonds. The trade gap widened 17 percent to $10.23 billion, exceeding the forecast $9.18 billion gap. April's trade deficit was revised to $8.75 billion from $8.36 billion.
The U.S.-Japan deficit fell 25 percent to $3.63 billion.
September T-bonds ended 15/32 lower at 114-06/32, 10-year notes were down 8/32 at 109-18/32, and March Eurodollars were down 0.025 basis points at 93.990.
